candidates.sourceHashScope: Captured .py files recursively within adapter directory; excludes dependencies and non-Python files.

cases.title: A lost response must not dispatch twice
cases.description: The fulfillment commits, then the response is lost. Redelivery and a new transport message for the same business order must reuse the receipt.

cases.title: Two orders with the same SKU both dispatch
cases.description: A second valid order is interleaved between a committed crash and redelivery of the first order. A SKU-only key wrongly suppresses the second order.

cases.title: Distinct shop references remain separate
cases.description: Identical product, quantity and shipping details still represent two valid business orders when the complete references differ.

cases.title: A reused reference cannot change its quantity
cases.description: After a successful dispatch, changed quantity under the same reference must be rejected. A later retry of the original payload remains reusable.

cases.title: Changed shipping is rejected after response loss
cases.description: The first dispatch commits before crashing. An altered destination is rejected under its existing reference, then the exact original payload retries successfully.

boundaries: Trusted local Python adapters only; defense-in-depth guard is not a hostile-code sandbox.
Receiver-owned simulated effects and bounded explicit schedules; no real AWS execution or cloud equivalence claimed.
Independent local receipts establish effects; handler returns do not.
Source hashes cover captured .py files in each adapter folder only; not signatures or dependency attestation.

guard.mechanism: CPython audit hook plus SDK/process/FFI import blocker
guard.boundary: Blocks normal Python socket, SDK, subprocess and ctypes paths; not a hostile-native-code sandbox.
